SURFER QUANTGOLD · BASIS STRATEGY

GoldOwl gold futures–spot basis strategy

GoldOwl tracks the difference between gold futures and spot prices, known as the basis. When it detects a divergence, it takes opposing positions. The result depends on convergence and the cost of both legs.

GoldOwlPartner strategy
01

Trading logic

If futures rise relative to spot, the basis widens. GoldOwl tracks that deviation and opens a futures–spot hedge when its conditions are met. If the basis then narrows, the relative movement between the two legs drives the result.

02

Risks & boundaries

The basis can keep widening. Different trading hours, thin liquidity or delays can leave one leg unfilled while the other is open. Spreads, fees and futures rolls all affect the net result.

03

Operating requirements

The source table lists XAUUSD, while the strategy also requires a gold futures leg. Deployment depends on the futures contract month, the size of both contracts, the hedge ratio and overlapping trading hours.
